senses.sense_definition: A long or complex journey or trip, often involving travel on foot.

examples.text: The author describes his long <w>peregrination</w> across the mountains in his latest travel memoir.
After years of <w>peregrination</w> through foreign lands, he finally decided to settle down in his hometown.

senses.sense_definition: A journey undertaken for religious or spiritual purposes; a pilgrimage.

examples.text: The monk began his spiritual <w>peregrination</w> to the holy site at the start of the spring season.
Many believers undertake a difficult <w>peregrination</w> to seek forgiveness and inner peace.

senses.sense_definition: The state of living or staying in a foreign country for a temporary period.

examples.text: During his long <w>peregrination</w> in France, he learned to speak the language fluently.
Her <w>peregrination</w> abroad provided her with a new perspective on her own culture.

senses.sense_definition: A straying from the main subject in speech or writing; a digression.

examples.text: The professor's lecture was filled with a confusing <w>peregrination</w> that distracted from the main topic.
Please avoid any unnecessary <w>peregrination</w> and stick to the facts of the case.

senses.sense_definition: A person's life viewed as a temporary stay on earth before the afterlife.

examples.text: The poet often wrote about human existence as a brief <w>peregrination</w> toward the divine.
He viewed his earthly <w>peregrination</w> as a time for moral growth and reflection.

traits.comment: Used in a literary or theological context.
